subject: Generated Quantities from a Log normal fit

messages.author: b2b2b752fe3de41b
messages.subject: Generated Quantities from a Log normal fit
parts:
I am running a updated version of the Clark triangle example referenced here:
https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/blob/master/vignettes/brms_nonlinear.Rmd

The goal is to estimate Loss ratio rather than ULT (ultimate losses). In addition, we data set has more variation than the clark triangle, and I think log normal would be a better fit than Gaussian. 
I therefore changed the model as below:

bf_formula_lnorm <- bf( TotalIncurred  ~ LR + log(OL_GWP) + log(1 - exp(-(dev/theta)^omega)),
                        LR ~ 1 + (1|Acc_Seg), omega ~ 1, theta ~ 1, 
                        nl = TRUE)

fit_BF_lnorm <- brm(bf_formula_lnorm,
                data = LR_SUMM, family = lognormal(),
                prior = c(prior(normal(0.6, 0.1), nlpar = "LR"),
                          prior(normal(2, 1), nlpar = "omega"),
                          prior(normal(45, 1), nlpar = "theta")),
                iter = 5000,
                control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9))

OL_GWP is the Premiums variable in the clark triangle example; Acc_Seg is a variable codes industry segments.
The model does converge. 

However, due to the nature of lognormal distribution, the loss ratio estimate I care about is really LR_real = exp(LR + LR_ranef + sigma^2/2)
Is there a way for me to extract the posterior distribution of LR_real from the brms fit object?

Thanks,
Allen

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: Generated Quantities from a Log normal fit
parts:
Provided I correctly understand your question, the following should work (assuming your model is named "fit"):

# LR + LR_ranef
LR_coef <- coef(fit, summary = FALSE)$Acc_Seg[, , "LR_Intercept"]
sigma <- as.numeric(as.matrix(fit, "^sigma$"))
# posterior samples
LR_real <- exp(LR_coef + sigma^2 / 2)
# extract summary statistics
brms:::get_summary(LR_real)


Best,
Paul
